name: Strawberry
grown_as: The garden strawberry, a perennial fruit kept by planting its runners. William's variety is not known; varieties differ little in leaf and flower.
habit: A low clump about 15 to 25 cm high and 30 to 45 cm across, from a short woody crown at ground level. No upright stem: every leaf and flower stalk rises straight from the crown. In summer it sends out long, thin, reddish runners along the ground, each rooting at a node to make a new plant.

leaf.arrangement: A loose rosette from the crown
leaf.type: Compound: three leaflets (trifoliate) from the top of one long stalk
leaf.leaflets: The middle leaflet on a very short stalk of its own and symmetrical; the two side leaflets with almost no stalk and lopsided, the outer half wider than the inner. The three meet neatly at the top of the stalk and touch or overlap a little at their bases.
leaf.outline: Each leaflet broadly oval to obovate (widest a little above the middle), 4 to 8 cm long, rounded at the tip
leaf.base: Each leaflet tapers to a wedge at its base
leaf.tip: Rounded, ending in a tooth as long as or longer than its neighbours
leaf.margin: Coarse, sharp teeth like a saw blade, pointing forward, along the upper two-thirds of each leaflet. The tapering base has no teeth.
leaf.veins: A midrib and 8 to 12 straight, parallel side veins on each side, each running out into a tooth. Deeply pressed in, so the leaflet looks pleated along them.
leaf.surface: Rich green and a little glossy above, paler and silky-hairy beneath
leaf.stalk: Long (10 to 20 cm), upright then arching, hairy, green or reddish
leaf.colour: Mid to dark green; some turn red in autumn and winter

flower.form: A flat open flower like a small wild rose
flower.petals: Five, free, white, round, not overlapping much
flower.centre: A raised yellow-green dome (the receptacle that becomes the fruit) dotted with tiny green pistils, ringed by about twenty yellow stamens
flower.behind: Ten green pointed sepals in two rings (five large, five small), showing between the petals
flower.carried: In small loose clusters on branched stalks from the crown, held among or just above the leaves, the flowers facing up or out
flower.season: May to June; some varieties again in late summer

fruit: The red swollen receptacle, cone-shaped to round, 2 to 5 cm, its surface covered in small yellow seeds (achenes) sitting in shallow pits. A ruff of green sepals at the top where it joins the stalk. Unripe fruit is white-green. The fruit hangs on its stalk, often resting on the ground or straw.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from runners or bought plants
winter: Evergreen in mild winters: a smaller rosette of a few leaves, the older ones turning red and brown, the crown showing at the soil.

leaf: three leaflets from the top of one stalk
each leaflet oval, widest above the middle, tapering to a wedge base
sharp teeth on the upper two-thirds only, none at the base
straight parallel side veins running into the teeth
bloom: a domed yellow-green centre ringed with yellow stamens
young: no stem: leaves on long stalks from a crown at the soil
each leaf the three-leaflet leaf of the close-up
flower: white flowers in small clusters on stalks from the crown, among the leaves
crop: red cone-shaped fruit with seeds on the surface and a green ruff
fruit hanging down to the soil on stalks
runner: a thin stalk running along the ground from the parent
a new small plant rooting where it touches down
dormant: a small low rosette of a few three-leaflet leaves, some reddened

look_alikes: Wild strawberry (Fragaria vesca) is smaller in every part with small fruit held above the leaves. Barren strawberry (Potentilla sterilis) has blue-green leaflets whose end tooth is shorter than its neighbours, petals with gaps between them, and dry fruit. Cinquefoils have five leaflets.
